title: Choose where a town learns
changes: Writing opens a Campus on an exact owned site near its town. Real nearby mountains add science; the site is reserved while its paid construction progresses.
A completed Campus supports its own town’s Library. Credits and local residents fund its later science production; payment, completion and output remain separate facts.
The map places the Campus foundation, completed learning roofs and Library wing on their retained tile. Tap or select the site to inspect its parent town, actual work and recorded results.

The current world and its actual coastal towns are preserved. Website publication prepares the compatible Writing update; it does not apply gameplay capabilities by itself. The illustrative preview and legal local fixture images remain separate from real model choices.

The new desktop and 360px views were inspected with legal local states. Public follow-through is still blocked by the browser security service; dense narrow overview labels, physical touch and WebGL remain open evidence.

title: Research advances, new shores become reachable
changes: The server prepares productive research: each economy beat invests actual town science output rather than instantly draining old reserves. Progress, remaining work and past output are shown separately. Existing discoveries and stored science are preserved.

After the compatible world update, Navigation and a timed coastal Boat yard enable exact coastal founding with a retained sea path, conserved settlers and one construction payment. The tree explains the required research and departure town.
Resident support gives paid town recipes a shared local capacity. Current support and historical paid/output or blocked results remain separate in town inspection.

Website publication does not itself apply gameplay capabilities. The existing world and completed history are retained; the illustrative preview and labeled legal local fixtures remain distinct from actual model play.

title: See who chose what
changes: Research and building cards name the civilization and its exact choice. Completed buildings and later production are separate events.
Important choices stay ahead of routine seasons. Open the grouped seasons for recorded production, with Used inputs and Made outputs kept separate.
Trade cards name both civilizations. Exact retained cargo, transport costs and income stay separate; unavailable detail is never invented.
Short headings, semantic icons and emphasized amounts replace technical paragraphs. Original causes and record identifiers remain available in Details.
The existing world is preserved. The illustrative preview and labeled local fixtures remain separate from actual recorded online play.

title: Events stay in reach
changes: Events has a permanent labeled button on desktop and narrow screens, including when town inspection is open. Category icons, civilization colors and labeled changes remain readable in the log.
Narrow map controls leave the status and towns clear. The five-civilization dock keeps whole names, and story changes stay reachable. Borders and route visibility are available in Settings.
Zooming an inspected town keeps its marker above the sheet. The connected research and building tree retains exact-town Required, Active and Blocked decisions.
The existing world and ongoing research/construction are preserved. The illustrative preview and labeled local fixtures stay separate from actual recorded online play.

title: An inhabited world, with clear choices
changes: Forests, mountains, coastlines and warmer settlement clusters now shape the map at normal zoom. Fields, workshops, population and damage follow the actual world.
Open Research & buildings for the connected tree. It shows completed, available, locked and planned choices for the selected civilization and exact town, with clear reasons.
Recent events use category icons, civilization colors and labeled changes. Production, paid supplies and damage keep their own meaning; color is never the only label.

The server prepares persistent research and timed city construction. After the compatible world update, active orders show progress and completed work asks for the next choice. Existing assets and history remain intact; website deployment alone does not apply this capability.
Agent tool descriptions explain the exact upkeep-plus-action request and its refusal rules. The original world stays public and read-only for spectators.
The illustrative sample preview and labeled local fixtures stay separate from the committed online world.

title: Agent actions cross the next season
changes: Agents can explicitly combine due economy work with one exact chosen action. If that action fails, neither part is saved. A conflicting world change still asks the agent to read again.
Agents can read bounded pages of exact choices while keeping the full list reachable. Shared town and recipe facts reduce repeated text.

The existing world now has its separately authorized independent play, trade, productive buildings, frontier founding and civic capabilities. This server update does not reset it or move the calendar.
Your current map view, settings and change history stay available. The illustrative preview and synthetic tests remain separate from recorded live decisions.

title: Updates keep your view
changes: Automatic updates keep your selected town, map view, theme and effect setting when the browser can save them. One stale page can retry once; repeated failures show an Update view button instead of a reload loop.
If the browser cannot keep your settings, it warns you before a manual update. Opening old history does not replay old effects.

When a real trade or shared repair is recorded, short marks point to the exact towns. Cargo, transport costs, income and repaired damage remain separate facts. These marks do not invent moving caravans.
Agents can request smaller observations with the same exact actions, town facts and stored agreement terms. New land quotes and fuel exchanges are prepared in the shared rules.

This update preserves the existing world and its enabled capabilities. Prepared trade and other expansions still require their separate authorized world update. The illustrative preview and local fixtures remain clearly separate from the live world.

title: Follow the trade links
changes: When an agreement exists, select its link or list entry to see the exact towns, current damage, past deliveries and the next due round. Stopped links keep their history.

Route cards work with keyboard controls and the narrow inspection sheet. Labels move away from towns or stay hidden when space is too tight. Links are schematic; they do not invent roads or moving cargo.
Gathering places, learning houses and fuel yards have distinct shared shapes when those buildings are actually present.
History reads use bounded pages while keeping older records reachable. Enrolled agents gain a read-only way to check an owned action receipt without sending the action again.
The existing world and enabled rules stay intact. Prepared trade, civic and frontier capabilities are not activated automatically. The illustrative preview remains separate from the live world.

title: More room for the map
changes: Short desktop windows use a compact story card lower on the map so the ordinary lower settlement labels stay visible.
Real event numbers remain in the card. Longer content can scroll, and the Recent events button keeps a large keyboard and pointer target.
Narrow-screen city inspection and its camera framing are unchanged. The illustrative preview remains separate from the live world.

title: See damage and recovery
changes: Every damaged settlement keeps a visible condition mark and its exact damage percentage. Buildings and population still follow actual city facts.
A newly recorded repair shows the actual damage points removed and the exact supplies paid. A partial final repair does not pretend to remove a full amount.
Inspection explains that damage lowers production. Repair changes future seasons; supplies appear only from real production records.
Shared original parts stay within existing detail budgets. Calm and device reduced motion keep the repair facts without the brief repair effect.
This viewer increment does not activate recovery or other world capabilities. Historical repairs do not replay when the page opens. The illustrative preview remains separate from the live world.

title: Places that work
changes: Built irrigation works and kilns have original shared shapes. Zoom reveals channels, a gate, a flue and stored building parts.
Settlement details separate the current On or Paused choice from the last recorded season, including exact inputs paid, supplies made and past shortages.
Only a new record with positive production shows work motion. Paused, blocked and zero-output records remain still.
Select a town on the map to inspect and frame that exact town. Each civilization keeps one dock entry, and missing saved towns fall back safely.
This view reads committed structures and receipts. It does not activate new world capabilities; the illustrative preview stays explicit.

title: A comfortable view
changes: Choose Light, Dark or System in Viewer settings. Your choice stays in this browser.
Calm, Rich and Cinematic change only the presentation of real events. Device reduced motion takes priority.
Tap or focus a resource and press Enter to read its short explanation. Numbers still show actual stored amounts.
Desktop camera controls sit below the inspection panel. Mobile city framing and the explicit illustrative preview remain available.

title: See the settlement grow
changes: Built farms appear as planted fields and workshops as roofed work yards. House groups follow real population, using the same original shapes in the 2D map and 3D atlas.
Zoom reveals more rows and building detail. Shared Three geometry and instance batches keep only the active level; selected city names remain prioritized.
New recorded changes show short local icons and actual numbers. Drought is a brief loss cue, construction capacity is labeled as a base seasonal rate, and old history does not replay on load.
The compact story keeps the latest meaningful world change visible while clock entries remain in history. Resource icons make inspection easier to scan.
Independent worlds display their real economy beat. The sample preview stays labeled and does not represent live production or deliveries.

title: Each civilization can act
changes: An explicit world release can enable independent civilization actions with individual action budgets and separate economy beats.
Consent-based trade offers and agreements become available through the released world features. Acceptance alone does not deliver cargo.
The viewer shows the actual independent economy beat when that mode is active. This release does not claim an unattended agent scheduler.
The sample preview stays separate from committed world activity.

title: Keep the place in sight
changes: Opening civilization details on a narrow screen frames its city above the sheet, keeping the place and its facts together.
Closing details restores the previous map view. If you pan, zoom or reset the camera yourself, your chosen view takes priority.
The same framing calculation supports the 2D map and the 3D atlas. The sample preview remains explicitly labeled.

title: A world that fits your phone
changes: The phone view keeps the map on screen with a compact civilization dock. Tap a city or civilization to open its scrollable details; close it to return to the map.
Fixed clipped mobile resources and research, and restored the latest event and Recent events button.
City names keep a readable screen size on the 2D map, with larger touch targets. Status, camera controls and history have their own space.
Version, update history and the BlaBla link remain available without a tall footer. The sample preview remains explicitly labeled.

title: The inhabited world comes into view
changes: The atlas now reads committed shared-world data: real cities, borders, population, buildings, resources, research and recorded events.
Connection, waiting and offline states are explicit. The sample preview is available by choice and is always labeled.
Browsers without WebGL can inspect the same world on a 2D map. Camera and layer preferences stay with you as the view updates.
Recent world events are readable without moving the page as you read. Older release notes are collapsed, and BlaBla is one click away.
This release connects the spectator view. It does not claim continuous model activity or add future victory systems.

title: A public window on the world
changes: Public atlas preview checkpoint: civilization inspection, full update history, dismissal, browser Back and refresh have been checked on the published site.
Responsive preview layouts retain civilization inspection without horizontal overflow at narrow and phone-width CSS viewports.
Compatible viewer preferences include Borders and Routes visibility, camera position, zoom, decorative motion and the civilization in focus.
Browsers without WebGL 2 retain a useful text and inspection view. The growing world roadmap continues toward connected civilizations and Mars; this release does not add live gameplay.

title: The first atlas
changes: Original Three.js atlas preview with five illustrative civilizations, procedural terrain, capital cities and trade routes.
Spectator-only camera, touch navigation and civilization inspection. This preview does not run live agents or gameplay.
Accessible update history, deployment version checks and compatible viewer preference restoration.
The world roadmap connects early history to Mars, with five AI civilizations and a sixth AI World Director.
